narrative: This daily brief highlights significant developments across technology, AI, infrastructure, and science. Key themes include the rapid evolution of AI agents, major updates in space technology, and crucial advancements in developer tools and scientific research.

highlights.title: Sometimes, a short game hits the spot
highlights.whyItMatters: Slots & Daggers, a low-key, fantasy-themed slot machine roguelike, was one of my favorite games last year.

highlights.title: The SpaceX IPO is great for Elon Musk and terrible for you
highlights.whyItMatters: I haven't seen anything as stupid as the WeWork IPO document in a very long time - that is, until Elon Musk filed to take SpaceX public.

highlights.title: Proposed new US funding rules: We can cancel any grant at any time
Show HN: Helios – what plug-in solar could generate for any address in Britain
highlights.whyItMatters: Plug-in solar panels (no electrician needed) have just become legal in the UK and will go on sale soon.

highlights.title: Grifters, cynics, and true believers: The family tree of vaccine opponents
highlights.whyItMatters: A new book looks into the long history of people who have opposed vaccines.

highlights.title: Leo's first encyclical attacks technological messianism
Founders seize on Indian court ruling to revive criticism of Google’s ad business
highlights.whyItMatters: The ruling drew support from founders, while lawyers said it could force platforms to revisit how they handle trademarked keywords.

highlights.title: I went to the so-called ‘steroid Olympics,’ to understand why Silicon Valley is obsessed with peptides
highlights.whyItMatters: The Enhanced Games — a singular sporting competition where a majority of the athletes were on performance enhancing drugs — may herald a new business model that the tech industry is ready to embrace.
